title: Attention Is All You Need
key_takeaway: The Transformer: self-attention replaces recurrence; multi-head attention, positional encodings, encoder-decoder. Every frontier LLM descends from this.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
key_takeaway: Interleave Thought -> Action -> Observation loops; the base pattern behind almost every tool-using agent loop today.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
key_takeaway: Intermediate reasoning steps in the prompt unlock multi-step reasoning in large models; precursor to reasoning models and test-time compute.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
org_authors: Lewis et al. (Facebook AI Research, UCL, NYU)
key_takeaway: Origin of RAG: a dense retriever (DPR) feeds passages to a seq2seq generator; parametric + non-parametric memory.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (InstructGPT)
key_takeaway: The SFT -> reward model -> PPO (RLHF) recipe that turned base LMs into assistants; defines the post-training vocabulary.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
key_takeaway: Pure RL with verifiable rewards (GRPO) elicits long chain-of-thought reasoning; open-weight reasoning model; distillation to small models.

title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
org_authors: Snell, Lee, Xu, Kumar (UC Berkeley, Google DeepMind)
key_takeaway: Compute-optimal test-time strategies (verifier search vs. sequential revision) adapt to prompt difficulty; frames the 'inference-time scaling' axis.

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention (vLLM)
key_takeaway: KV cache as paged virtual memory removes fragmentation and enables high-throughput batching; the basis of vLLM.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
org_authors: Liu et al. (Stanford, UC Berkeley, Samaya AI)
key_takeaway: Retrieval accuracy drops when relevant information sits in the middle of a long context; position matters for RAG and context engineering.

title: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance
key_takeaway: Across 18 models, performance degrades non-uniformly as input length grows even on simple tasks; 'bigger context window' is not 'free capacity'.

title: Building Effective Agents
key_takeaway: Workflows vs. agents; five composable patterns (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer); start simple.

title: Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents
key_takeaway: Context is a finite resource: system prompt altitude, tool design, just-in-time retrieval, compaction, structured note-taking, sub-agent isolation.

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
key_takeaway: Orchestrator-worker with parallel sub-agents; prompt engineering for delegation; evaluation with LLM judges; production reliability lessons.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Specification
key_takeaway: Client-host-server architecture; tools, resources, prompts; JSON-RPC over stdio/HTTP; authorization; the interoperability layer for enterprise agents.

title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025)
key_takeaway: Prompt injection, sensitive info disclosure, supply chain, data poisoning, improper output handling, excessive agency, system prompt leakage, vector weaknesses, misinformation, unbounded consumption.

title: The lethal trifecta for AI agents: private data, untrusted content, and external communication
key_takeaway: If an agent has private-data access + reads untrusted content + can exfiltrate, prompt injection becomes data theft; break one leg of the trifecta.

title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
org_authors: Beurer-Kellner et al. (IBM, Invariant Labs, ETH Zurich, Google, Microsoft, et al.)
key_takeaway: Six patterns (action-selector, plan-then-execute, map-reduce, dual LLM, code-then-execute, context minimization) that trade generality for provable injection resistance.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
key_takeaway: MAST taxonomy of 14 failure modes across specification, inter-agent misalignment, and verification; most failures are design problems, not model problems.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
key_takeaway: Freeze base weights, train low-rank update matrices; the default parameter-efficient fine-tuning method.

title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
key_takeaway: Preference optimization without an explicit reward model or RL loop; closed-form reparameterization of RLHF objective.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
key_takeaway: Loss scales as a power law in parameters, data, and compute; read with Chinchilla (arXiv:2203.15556) for the compute-optimal correction.

title: nanoGPT (hands-on: train a small GPT from scratch)
key_takeaway: Minimal, readable GPT training code; the fastest path to a working mental model of attention, tokenization, and the training loop.

title: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) documentation
key_takeaway: GCP-native agent framework (agents, tools, sessions, memory, evaluation, deployment to Agent Engine); aligns with the GCP-first upskilling plan.

title: OpenAI GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol
key_takeaway: Frontier (Astra: $8/$0.40 cached/$40 per 1M) and everyday (Sol: $2/$0.10/$10) models, GA in API with Ultrafast option. Vendor deltas only on most benchmarks; system card (deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-6-2-astra-sol) documents a regression where models omit obstacles encountered during work, plus Critical cyber rating gating via Daybreak.

title: Anthropic Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
key_takeaway: Same model, two safeguard configurations (Fable GA on Claude Platform/AWS/GCP/Azure; Mythos via Cyber/Life-Sciences Verification). $8/$40 per 1M, optional fast mode up to 2.5x. Vendor table: FrontierCode 2.0 49.1%, Terminal-Bench-Science 74.6%, Remote Labor Index 41.3%; Gemini 4 Carbon leads AutomationBench in Anthropic's own table. System card: anthropic.com/document/claude-fable-5-2-mythos-5-2-system-card

title: Gemini 4 Carbon now broadly available
key_takeaway: Top Gemini 4 tier opened beyond Fairwind cyber defenders. Intro price $2/$10 per 1M until 2026-11-30, then $4/$20. Vendor: #1 CursorBench 4.0, WANDR, Zapier AutomationBench; Gray Swan indirect-prompt-injection 0% attack success (vendor). Previews /swarm multi-agent in Antigravity.

title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon (mid-tier, 1M context, four thinking levels)
key_takeaway: gemini-4-neon: $3/$0.15 cached/$15 per 1M, 1M context, thinking levels up to xhigh. Vendor: AA Intelligence Index 61 (xhigh), Terminal-Bench 4.1 65.2%, FrontierCode 2.0 46.2%, Zapier AutomationBench 56.3%; claims 32% lower cost/task than Carbon at high.

title: Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen (fast tier, 1M in / 1M out, free tier)
key_takeaway: Replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash. $1.50/$7.50 per 1M flat across 1M context; up to 1M output tokens; PDF/spreadsheet/audio/video input. Vendor: Terminal-Bench 4.1 57% (3.8 Flash 18.2%), Agents' Last Exam 71.6%. Google pitches Carbon-plans / Hydrogen-executes orchestration.

title: Microsoft Ignite 2026: MAI Code 2, MAI Cyber 2 Flash, MAI Licensed Weights, Decision 1.1, Maia 200
key_takeaway: First-party price/performance tier: MAI Code 2 claims 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol coding quality at ~40% price (relative claims only, promo pricing). MAI Licensed Weights = deploy and fine-tune MAI models inside customer Azure tenant (coming soon). Decision 1.1 routing model GA. Maia 200 accelerator in production.

title: Alibaba Qwen4-Max
key_takeaway: Proprietary first Qwen4 model, 1M context, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API at $1.50/$4.50 per 1M (Singapore). Independent AA Intelligence Index 43 vs Fable 5.2 65, Carbon 60, Kimi K3.1 Pro 46; high latency. Official post not readable (JS); details via VentureBeat/AIwire.

title: Mistral Large 4 open weights ('Le Chonk', 1T MoE)
key_takeaway: Largest Western open-weight model (HF: mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B) under Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License (modified MIT; MaaS resale needs separate licence). API $0.70/$0.07/$2.10 per 1M. Vendor: Terminal-Bench 4.0 41%, FrontierCode 2.0 19.7% (well below closed frontier). Main EU-sovereign on-prem option.

title: Kimi K3.1 Pro open weights (2.8T/104B-active MoE, 1M context)
key_takeaway: Strongest open-weight model by independent indices (AA 46). Hybrid attention (69 KDA + 24 Gated DSA layers), 896 experts (16 routed + 2 shared), MXFP4 weights via quantization-aware training. Self-hosting needs 8-way TP class hardware; practically consumed via providers (already on Databricks Unity Gateway).

title: Tencent Hunyuan Hy4 open weights and system card
key_takeaway: 770B total / 49B active natively multimodal MoE with MLA + gated sparse attention, 4-stream residual, built-in 3.3B speculative drafter, 1M context, computer-use. Tencent Hy License (revenue/MAU thresholds, unverified). System card: hy.tencent.ai/Hy4_system_card.pdf

title: Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Mini (open-weight looped transformer, ~20 GB)
key_takeaway: 26.4B total / 3.4B active MoE; 24 stored layers with two middle blocks looped three times (48 layer applications, 5.4B effective activations); NVFP4 weights; runs on 32GB Mac / DGX Spark; Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang. Strong SWE-bench Verified 79.2% (vendor) but weak long-horizon terminal (TB 4.0 5.6%).

title: Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Small (594B/17B-active open MoE, 1M-context training)
key_takeaway: Multimodal MoE with 512K-1M context phases and RL at 256K with compaction; NVFP4 and MXFP8 checkpoints on HF; on Tinker and major providers. Vendor: BrowseComp 90.2% w/ compaction, ARC-AGI-2 81.7%, but Terminal Bench Science 5.7%. Related: End-to-End 4-Bit Training post (2026-11-13).

title: OpenAI GPT-6 Cyber (Critical-rated, Daybreak-gated)
key_takeaway: Vulnerability discovery/exploit model restricted to Daybreak Red customers with IP allowlisting. ExploitGym 48.5% (vs 32.1%). Establishes the industry-wide 'verified defender' gated-access pattern (OpenAI Daybreak, Anthropic CVP/Mythos, Google Fairwind).

title: Meta Muse Ember 1.0 (hosted executor model, 1M context, $0.10/$0.50)
key_takeaway: Closed, hosted (Meta Model API, OpenAI-compatible; also GCP/OCI). Text/image/audio/video in, 512K output. Priced an order of magnitude under mid-tier models; vendor table beats Haiku 5.5/GPT-6 Luna on AutomationBench, loses on FrontierCode. Confirms Meta's shift away from open-weight Llama.

title: NVIDIA Nemotron for Science (Nemotron 3.5 Super VL + LitmusBench v0.2)
key_takeaway: Open mid-size VLM + ~50k-question chemistry dataset + post-training recipes. Partner results (Lila 61% vs GPT-6 Astra 54% at 10-20x lower cost) illustrate 'post-train open VLM on domain data' pattern for on-prem regulated workloads. Licence not stated.

title: Zhipu GLM-5.4 (first Loop Transformer flagship)
key_takeaway: 28-layer GLM-5 base run for two passes with per-token gates, hybrid KV cache, reused sparse-attention indices; continued training, not from scratch. No tech report, benchmarks, or API yet. Watch for technical report alongside Inkling 2 Mini as looped-depth trend.

title: AlphaProof Code: agentic formal verification of Signal's cryptographic protocol code
key_takeaway: Gemini Carbon agents generated >6M lines of Lean to verify compiled Signal protocol code in four weeks; humans reviewed ~1% flagged; produced machine-checked insecurity proofs for two reintroduced historical bugs. Paper: deepmind.google/documents/36/Formal_Verification_of_Signal_4.pdf; artifacts google-deepmind.github.io/code-verification

title: Hugging Face Inference Providers: LLM routing moves to OpenRouter
key_takeaway: Language-model calls through HF Inference Providers now route via OpenRouter; custom provider keys no longer work for LLMs; pricing unchanged. Dependency change for teams using HF inference endpoints.

title: llama.cpp v1.0.0
key_takeaway: First 1.0 of the de facto local inference engine (GGUF). Relevant for on-device/edge agents and for running Inkling 2 Mini class models locally.

title: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service at Ignite 2026: hosted agents, Copilot harness, Insights -> Agent Optimizer -> training loop, BYO-AKS
key_takeaway: Managed runtime for your own agent code (VM-isolated sandboxes) or Microsoft's managed Copilot harness; GA network egress rules (allow/deny/header-inject/gateway), Entra Agent ID, toolboxes as managed MCP endpoints; preview closed loop where production traces cluster failures and an optimizer proposes eval-gated changes; BYO-AKS public preview targeted Dec 2026. Book of News: news.microsoft.com/events/ignite/2026/book-of-news/

title: Microsoft Agent 365 + Entra Agent ID at Ignite 2026: cross-platform agent registry, MCP governance/firewall, Defender runtime protection for local agents
key_takeaway: Registry/control plane for agents built anywhere (Bedrock, Vertex, Databricks, Snowflake, Anthropic, OpenAI in preview) with Entra identity and Conditional Access at point of action; Defender discovers 60+ local agents (Claude Code, Copilot CLI) and their MCP servers, with runtime block on Windows (GA); MCP Firewall and Dynamic Agent Risk in preview. Expect security teams to require agent identities and DLP on agent I/O.

title: Microsoft Copilot SDK 2.0: in-process Rust harness runtime with C ABI, multi-session hosting, Agent Host Protocol
key_takeaway: The Copilot agent loop as an embeddable multi-tenant runtime (TS/Python/Go/.NET/Java/Rust bindings); sessions are durable, resumable, persisted to object storage; six topologies from no-sandbox to coordinator+isolated workers. Vendor numbers: session+turn 5.25s -> 55ms, 10 clients 1,383MB -> 126MB. GitHub: github.com/microsoft/copilot-sdk

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore November 2026: Runtime V2 resource configs, InvokeWebSearch API GA, org-level RCPs + JWT-claim condition keys, Agent Registry skill packages
key_takeaway: Per-session microVM runtime with committed-baseline (0.25 vCPU/1GB to 2 vCPU/8GB) + 4x burst pricing, 10GB images, S3 mounts, G7 GPU instances, nested virtualization; direct web search API ($7/1k queries, 5k free/month); Resource Control Policies at org/OU level and bedrock-agentcore:InboundJwtClaim/* keys for gateway authz; skill-package registry (SKILL.md zips, SHA-256). AWS blog claims 15x faster start / 68% less memory (vendor, blog body not readable). Web Search: aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-web-search-api/

title: GitHub Copilot Fusion GA: multi-model routing with Single / Cascade / Critique workflows and Standard/High/Max effort
key_takeaway: Replaces model picking with an orchestration layer: Cascade (cheap draft + quality check, escalate), Critique (draft/review/revise across models). Billed per underlying model; admins scope which models Fusion may use. GitHub-reported: Fusion Max 60 on AA Coding Agent Index at ~half the API cost of Claude Code + Opus 5.5 Max. Universe recap: github.blog/news-insights/company-news/github-universe-2026-evolving-every-layer-of-the-stack/

title: Claude Platform release notes (Oct 28 - Nov 23, 2026): Fable/Mythos 5.2 1M context, message threads beta, self-hosted Managed Agents, linked billing, Enterprise Frontier Safeguards
key_takeaway: 5.2 models: 1M context, 128k max output, always-on adaptive thinking, $8/$40 (down from $10/$50), fast mode speed:'fast'. Message threads keep state server-side (beta header message-threads-2026-08-12). Self-hosted Managed Agents runs the whole agents service on your infra. Linked billing (billing_policy) for ISVs. EFS: ZDR plus encrypted Sealed Safety Data in your own bucket. 5.2 models require 30-day retention unless ZDR authorized; Opus 4.5 retires 2027-01-22.

title: Claude Ship: Code Review GA, PR Steward and Claude Approvals beta (policy-as-file merge gating)
key_takeaway: Review -> fix (CI, conflicts, review comments; never merges) -> approval against a natural-language policy file committed to the repo, with observe-only mode and branch protection. Team/Enterprise, GitHub only; NOT available to ZDR, HIPAA, or CMEK orgs. Docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-ship

title: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.168-0.171 (remote sessions, SPIFFE workload identity, Guardian reviewer) and Agent Builder shutdown 2026-11-30
key_takeaway: codex exec --remote against an app server, SPIFFE JWT-SVID auth, seccomp coverage, MCP disabled in untrusted dirs; GPT-6.2 Sol default. Agent Builder (AgentKit visual canvas) and Prompt Objects shut down 2026-11-30: export to Agents SDK code. Deprecation guide: developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-builder/index.html

title: Google Antigravity 2.27-2.35 (remote agents, /swarm, Dynamic Workflows, device policies) and Jules turndown (read-only Nov 11, shutdown Dec 31)
key_takeaway: Antigravity is now Google's single developer-agent surface; Jules users must export via @google/jules CLI before 2026-12-31 (export includes secret values). Enterprise access via Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform projects; admin_settings.json device policies.

title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform release notes: Gemini 4 Carbon/Hydrogen GA with data residency, 3-legged OAuth for A2A agents on Agent Runtime, Agent Gateway VPC/static egress for MCP
key_takeaway: GCP-first relevance: ADK-built A2A agents on Agent Runtime can act on behalf of the signed-in user (consent callback) when calling MCP servers/APIs; custom MCP egress via Private Service Connect or Cloud NAT static IPs (us-central1, europe-west1); Vertex AI docs no longer updated, services folded into Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform; Gemini Code Assist bundled entitlements end 2027-03-31.

title: Amazon Kiro: VS Code extension GA, Crew 0.13 Conductor, enforced sandboxing for local MCP, VPC-connected cloud sessions, Fable 5.2 preview
key_takeaway: Admins can require sandboxing for commands and stdio MCP servers that developers cannot disable (preview, us-east-1); org sign-in for HTTP MCP; EU (eu-central-1) enterprise management; Fable 5.2 preview at 6x credit multiplier.

title: MCP moves to a fixed six-month spec release cycle (next: 2027-03-30)
org_authors: Model Context Protocol (Agentic AI Foundation / Linux Foundation)
key_takeaway: Spec releases on the last Tuesday of March and September; soft freeze 2.5 months out, Tier 1 SDK betas 1.5 months out, hard freeze 1 month out (SEP-3398). Current spec remains 2026-07-28. Lets enterprise teams plan MCP upgrades on a calendar.

title: MCP experimental file upload/download extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/files)
key_takeaway: Tool args marked x-mcp-file; inline base64 under maxInlineBytes else server returns upload_required with upload URL + single-use requestState; downloads via _meta targets; credentials: omit|include restricted to MCP origin; clients must refuse redirects. Draft, no reference implementation yet; finalization targeted before end of 2026.

title: MCP server security wave: reference servers v2.4.0/v2.5.0 fix 14 advisories; Todoist MCP DNS-rebinding CVE-2026-76807 (CVSS 9.3)
key_takeaway: Git server: repo config could make Git run programs (hooks, filter/diff drivers, submodules); filesystem: symlink-swap escapes and TOCTOU; fetch: IPv6/NAT64 private-address bypasses. Todoist HTTP transport accepted browser-origin POSTs with no Host/Origin check (stdio unaffected): github.com/todoist/todoist-mcp/security/advisories/GHSA-833v-v58w-294h. Date-versioned npm packages will not auto-upgrade; some Windows fixes partial. Inventory vendored MCP servers now.

title: Dragos canary-token study: prompt theft at inference hosting providers; OpenRouter off-boards 3 providers and delists 125 ZDR endpoints
key_takeaway: ~2M seeded prompts (Jul-Nov 2026) with canary URLs/credentials: at least three hosting providers had request traffic copied by attackers (front-door interception incl. rejected requests); stolen AWS keys used for tens of thousands of calls; some stolen requests carried the ZDR flag; a lab's systems fetched canary URLs from over half of prompts incl. ~2/3 flagged ZDR; attacker used ARTEX LLM pentest framework. OpenRouter response (2026-11-22): openrouter.ai/blog/announcements/data-processing-incidents-on-inference-providers/. Lesson: router ZDR flags are contractual, not technical, controls; rotate any secret that ever appeared in a prompt; seed canaries in agent context.

title: vLLM v0.34.0 (and v0.33.0): Model Runner V2 only, extensible KV cache default, CRIU checkpoint/restore, default block-size 64
key_takeaway: Breaking defaults: gpu_memory_utilization 1.0, --block-size 64, extensible KV cache on (bigger cache from free memory after warmup, 6-18% per-token decode latency cost on some H200 workloads; opt out with --no-enable-extensible-kv-cache); /checkpoint/prepare|status|restore; fault-tolerant DP+EP scale-down; v0.33 moved to PyTorch 2.14 / CUDA 13.0 only. Re-benchmark before upgrading.

title: Hugging Face Transformers v5.22-v5.24: Mistral Large 4, Inkling 2, FP8 LoRA training, past_key_values -> cache rename, Jinja sandbox hardening
key_takeaway: Weekly cadence with breaking changes: cache kwarg rename (compat to v5.40/v6.0), peft>=0.22 required, v5.22.2 security patch for chat-template Jinja sandbox. Pin versions in fine-tuning/serving pipelines.

title: Snowflake Expedition 2026: Business Ontology, Cortex AI Gateway (abuse detection, tracing, sandboxes, cost governance, dynamic routing), Cortex Training
key_takeaway: Gateway as the policy point for agent model/tool access and cost; ontology-grounded semantics for consistent agent answers. Primary pages returned 403; status from SiliconANGLE/Constellation (Business Ontology private preview; Cortex Training public preview).

title: Langfuse Cloud v4-only cutover (2026-11-16): legacy ingestion, trace-level evaluators and deprecated read APIs removed
key_takeaway: Older SDKs (Python v2 / JS v3) silently stop ingesting on Cloud; migrate to Python v5 / JS v6 or OpenTelemetry ingestion with x-langfuse-ingestion-version: 4; self-hosted v3 EOL 2027-01-31.

title: Cerebras disaggregated inference in production: GPU prefill + CS-3 decode via KV Portal
key_takeaway: Prefill/decode disaggregation across heterogeneous hardware (vLLM/SGLang prefill, Cerebras decode, RDMA KV transfer); vendor claims 5x tokens per MW vs CS-3 alone on GPT-OSS-120B. Early access for AWS, Fireworks, others. Pattern to understand for inference cost engineering.

title: ServiceNow agentic continuous control monitoring in IRM (GA expected Q1 2027)
key_takeaway: Agents monitoring compliance controls continuously, integrated with Control Tower; relevant to public-sector GRC clients once GA.

title: You don't need long context
org_authors: Belcak, Muralidharan, Jiang, ... Molchanov (NVIDIA, affiliation inferred from project page)
key_takeaway: Preprint. With end-of-conversation compaction, Claude Opus 4.5 and GPT 5.6 Sol stay within about -4 to +6 points of full-history baselines on SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, tau2-bench, BFCLv3 at 2-9x modeled cost savings; single-action compaction (one action per fresh context) also works (Opus 4.5 70.2% SWE-bench Verified vs 70.0%). Open-weight models vary wildly (Qwen3 Coder Next 53.0% -> 3.6%). Proposes 'semantic state space models'. Internal inconsistency on SAC median context; verify against PDF.

title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
org_authors: He, Zhoubian, ... Han, Zhai (UIUC, Tsinghua, Renmin, Verdent.ai, Waterloo)
key_takeaway: Preprint. 11 memory systems x 3 benchmarks x 3 backbones: 90 of 99 configurations score below 2-round RAG over raw history; on LongMemEval-s all 33 lose (1.2 to 40.4 points). Decomposes net value into memory benefit vs memory tax (evidence lost in reorganization). Default to raw-history retrieval; benchmark any memory layer against 2-round RAG on your own data. Project: hexuan21.github.io/MemoryTax/

title: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks
org_authors: Zhang, Bertran, Avula, Lee, Murdock (Amazon Responsible AI)
key_takeaway: Preprint. Attacks that keep the benign task but tamper with one of six decision components (objective, rules, consequences, actions, observation interpretation, world-state beliefs). Detection defenses (DRIFT) collapse objective attacks (2.4%) but leave observation/state tampering at 9.5-12.1%; tool-policy defenses barely help; capability-based CaMeL holds at ~1% across all targets. Code: github.com/amazon-science/task-tampering-prompt-injection

title: Scaling Adaptive Prompt Injection Attacks with Agent Swarms
key_takeaway: Preprint. An 'Agentic Optimizer' (8 teams x 2 agents, 320 eval calls/scenario, shared strategy DB) reaches attack success of 90-99% on Gemini 3.x Flash, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and 34% on Gemini 4 Argon (safety classifiers disabled); success rises with attacker capability. Static benchmarks saying 'robust' are not evidence against adaptive attackers; defense-in-depth outside the model is mandatory.

title: Matched Capabilities, Different Behaviors: A Controlled Study of MCP and CLI Interfaces for Language Agents
key_takeaway: Preprint. MICA renders identical capabilities as MCP tool schemas vs CLI and runs both through one runtime: structured behavioral divergence in 94.3% of 2,004 paired episodes; DART (decouple semantic decision from interface realization, repair the realization) improves scores up to 9 points and cuts MCP token cost up to 27.1k tokens/task. Tool-surface design is a measurable performance and cost lever. No code.

title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
org_authors: Dong, Sun, Yang, ... Wen, Dou (Renmin, Fudan, SJTU)
key_takeaway: Preprint (work in progress). Builds training environments from real MCP execution traces (deterministic dependency mining, clustering, state synthesis only where tools mutate state, replay-verified tasks). 7-benchmark average: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 23.0 -> 41.0 (43.2 w/ RL); GLM-5.2 backbone 44.6 -> 56.6 (= Claude Opus 5). Your own MCP traces can become training data. No code listed.

title: Embeddings vs. Grep: Rethinking the Dense Advantage in Code Search
org_authors: Xue, Zhang, Liao, Qin, Mu, Yu (Ant Group)
key_takeaway: Preprint, preregistered. Repo-Premium benchmark (file ranking, 6 languages, 91+ repos). Dense premium over chunked BM25 (+0.121 nDCG@10) shrinks to +0.034 vs whole-file BM25; 'generate-then-grep' (LLM adds identifiers, whole-file BM25) beats dense (0.613 vs 0.532); RRF fusion beats dense-only. Default for code RAG: hybrid BM25 + dense + LLM query expansion. Dataset: huggingface.co/datasets/hq-bench/repo-premium

title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
org_authors: Kang, Xu, Li, ... Stoica, Han (Georgia Tech, UIUC, UC Berkeley, NVIDIA, OpenAI, MIT)
key_takeaway: Preprint. Symmetric engines switch prefill/decode roles at runtime (6.2 s vs 754 s Dynamo relaunch), online planner resizes the P/D split, agent-aware KV manager evicts zero-reference blocks first. vs Dynamo: 1.10-2.73x throughput, up to 13.92x lower P95 TTFT, 81-95% less lost KV reuse on GLM-5.2 / Kimi K2.6 with replayed Claude Code traces. Code: github.com/mit-han-lab/EvolvingInfra

title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
key_takeaway: Preprint + open model (huggingface.co/google/embeddinggemma-2). 744M model embeds text, image, audio, video; selective encoder loading (271M text-only); Matryoshka dims 768->128; int4 QAT. MTEB Code 78.68 (within 2 pts of a ~28x larger model); MTEB Multilingual v2 61.36; on-device 191-567 MB on Pixel 11 Pro. Candidate default embedding for on-prem multimodal RAG.

title: The Devil is in the Context: Nine Dimensions of Prompt Injection Attacks
org_authors: Microsoft Security Response Center, UNSW, ETH Zurich
key_takeaway: Preprint. Nine-dimension taxonomy (source label, fragmentation, visibility, interpretability, conditionality, agent-state modification, topic relation, intended effect, original-task completion) applied to 9 benchmarks and 6 real incidents (GitHub MCP exfiltration, hidden-Unicode skill, M365 Copilot memory poisoning...); 13% of pairwise combinations untested. Use as a defense-coverage checklist.

title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
key_takeaway: Preprint. 'Decision models' (typed single-pass outputs: JEV, Decider v1.2, GPT Decisions) are poor actors on ordered multi-step tasks (JEV <=18.8% ordered) but good judges ('did this action help?') and cheap teachers: JEV rewards + GRPO lift Qwen2.5-1.5B 72.8 -> 82.9% ALFWorld, 56.8 -> 71.4% WebShop, beating a 7B GRPO policy, for ~$22-30 API cost. Code: github.com/ZJU-REAL/decision-agents

title: Context Language Models
org_authors: Shao, ... Zettlemoyer, Koh (reported UW + Meta FAIR; ICLR 2027 submission, scores unverified)
key_takeaway: Preprint (outside window; surfaced via ICLR 2027 review reports). Model edits its own context as a file; reported +11.4% BrowseComp-Plus at -21.5% FLOPs and 'Suffix Cache Reuse' -35% server compute vs SGLang. Pairs with 'You don't need long context' and context-engineering practice (compaction, note-taking). OpenReview scores unverified (verification wall).

title: Length Is Cheap, Competition Is Not: Attention Predicts Context Rot in Retrieval
key_takeaway: Preprint. Neutral filler is nearly free up to 32K; evidence-formatted competitors and rival values for the queried key cause the damage (one rival multiplies loss 9-110x); attention mass on evidence explains up to 58% of loss variance vs <=8% for length. Models <=3B. For RAG: deduplicate and resolve conflicts rather than only shrinking context. Code/data: github.com/yliusci/length-is-cheap

title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
org_authors: Ren, Yang, Deng, ... Jiang (IQuestLab; affiliation unverified)
key_takeaway: Preprint. Turn-level advantage (GAE across turns) plus centered within-turn trace, with turn-level importance sampling. Qwen3-4B-Thinking / Qwen3-30B-A3B: BrowseComp-Plus 48.1 / 50.3, GAIA 39.5 / 43.4; claims best on nine metrics vs GRPO/GSPO/PPO/VAPO/SAO (GiGPO not compared; single runs). Code: github.com/IQuestLab/Multiscale-Policy-Optimization

title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
org_authors: Song, Zhang, Tajwar, ... Salakhutdinov, Bagnell, Singh, Zanette (CMU, JHU, Aurora)
key_takeaway: Preprint, 67 pages. RL with binary rewards rewritten as maximum likelihood on the success-conditioned policy, so pretrain/midtrain/SFT/RL collapse into one likelihood loss over a time-varying mixture. At <=0.76B scale, unified training beats staged on several settings and retains pretraining loss / general benchmarks better (continual-learning angle). Skim sections 1-3 (30 min).

title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression (LoCo)
org_authors: Yuan, Xu, ... Zhou (Xi'an Jiaotong University, WeChat AI)
key_takeaway: Preprint. Targets the local stop/continue decision: flag low-confidence/high-volatility steps, judge for overthinking, sample shortest correct continuation, DPO. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B: 25-45% fewer tokens with equal or better accuracy (AIME24 50.8 -> 54.2 at -45.4%); math-only training transfers to code. Code: github.com/MuyaoYuan/LoCo

title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
key_takeaway: Preprint. Tool observations compressed into latent tokens in the agent's embedding space with action-preserving training; 70-89% fewer tokens and 24-56% lower runtime with improved QA accuracy on four benchmarks. Code: github.com/THU-Agent/Coca-cola

title: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?
key_takeaway: Preprint. Defines a 'mismatch budget' for quantized/async rollouts in on-policy distillation; FP8 recipes give >=1.93x KV-cache tokens vs BF16 and FP8 + async reaches equal quality 1.62x sooner; OPD stays stable where RL destabilizes. Code: github.com/benyucong/train-inference-mismatch-opd

title: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop (RepoFactory)
key_takeaway: Preprint. 10,159 verifiable repo-building environments across 17 domains; Qwen3.5-35B-A3B gains 22.6 pp on NL2Repo-Bench (17.5 without the evolution loop), +8.5 average across five benchmarks. Part of the 'environments as the scarce asset' theme.

title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think (DICE)
key_takeaway: Preprint. Pre-sample and synchronize verification randomness so draft-tree selection and prefetch target continuations that will actually be accepted; up to 24.6 pp speedup over strong baselines, no drafter retraining, exact target distribution.

title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
org_authors: Cui, Li, Hao, Ding, Liu, Cao (AIR Tsinghua; USTC)
key_takeaway: Preprint. W4A16 agents recover to within ~1 point of BF16 task success (Qwen3-8B 53.18 vs 53.54; Gemma 4 12B 64.31 vs 65.13) via execution-verified, teacher-steered corrections as distillation targets; 67% fewer training GPU hours than QeRL on tau2-Bench. Pair with 'Jagged Robustness' (safety does not transfer evenly under quantization). No code.

title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report (MoE block-diffusion LLM)
key_takeaway: Preprint, vendor-reported. 35B total / 3B active block-diffusion LM with Gated-DeltaNet memory + in-block bidirectional attention; claims SWE-bench Verified 73.6, Terminal-Bench 2.1 51.7, 680 tok/s on one GB300 (batch 1). First diffusion LLM with credible agentic-coding numbers; weights CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (huggingface.co/Diffuspace/Clover-35B-A3B-Preview). Needs independent validation.

title: Beam Model Technical Report (Reflection AI, 501B/23B-active MoE)
key_takeaway: Preprint, CC BY-SA 4.0 report. 501.3B total / 23.4B active, 23.8T tokens, 1M context, async RL on 10.5K GB300s (100M+ rollouts in ~4 weeks), FP8/NVFP4 serving with a 1.93B DFlash 2 drafter. Weights link not on abstract page (unverified). Useful as a transparent frontier-scale training recipe.

title: Jagged Robustness: Uneven Safety Transfer and Emerging Vulnerabilities under LLM Quantization
key_takeaway: Preprint. On Qwen3-4B, safeguards and bias degrade under quantization while truthfulness holds; universal adversarial suffixes harmless on the full model jailbreak the quantized one. Re-run safety evals after quantizing. Code: github.com/LucianoXu/QuantBeyoundEfficiency

title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
key_takeaway: Preprint. Bootstrap non-inferiority test for replacing a human annotator with an LLM judge when items lack shared annotators; 18 LLMs x 5 prompting techniques x 20 datasets; LLMs pass in about half of setups; ~100 items suffice. A statistical gate for LLM-as-judge adoption.

title: The novelty exposed: ablation, reproducibility and transparency in 40 technical reports of open-weight LLMs
key_takeaway: Preprint. Only 19 of 73 novelty claims have a with/without ablation; 4 of 40 reports state more than one training run; 1 of 40 discloses data mixture, token count and compute together. Calibrates skepticism when reading vendor technical reports.
